title: WHO gives meal counts that rise from the first tastes to the second year
summary: The infant-feeding sheet says 2 to 3 meals a day at 6 to 8 months, and 3 to 4 meals at 9 to 23 months, plus snacks.
body: The 4 August 2026 infant and young child feeding fact sheet says the number of times a child is fed should increase with age. It states 2 to 3 meals per day for infants 6 to 8 months of age, and 3 to 4 meals per day for infants 9 to 23 months of age, with 1 to 2 additional snacks as required. Breastfeeding continues in the same set of principles. These counts are the sheet's guidance for complementary feeding. They are not a record of what a particular kitchen serves, and snack means an extra eating time on that sheet, not a brand of food.
